bug_semantics: cqlsh records every executed statement in a local readline history file and never redacts secrets. Commands such as LOGIN <user> '<password>', CREATE/ALTER USER|ROLE ... WITH PASSWORD, and other password-bearing CQL therefore persist in cleartext in ~/.cassandra/cqlsh_history (migrated from ~/.cqlsh_history). Anyone with local read access to that file recovers prior-session credentials. CVE.org and Apache (CASSANDRA-21180 / oss-security) treat this as a real CWE-532 leak in Cassandra 4.0.0–4.0.19, not a withdrawn or rejected record. The 4.0.20 vendor patch does not strip passwords from history; it adds --disable-history / cqlshrc [history] disabled=true, skips readline.write_history_file when disabled, and prints a warning that history may contain passwords.
flaw_origin: The leak is the original unredacted history sink, not the later path rename. CASSANDRA-3188 (1bb2947dd58101ae185d7f2fe309c5dd5f6a44df, 2011-11-07) first added next-gen cqlsh as bin/cqlsh with HISTORY=~/.cqlsh_history and readline.write_history_file(HISTORY) on exit. Immediate parent 51a236c48e8a1d3e4b8d26b33942557fe5749f2c has no bin/cqlsh and no write_history_file anywhere. Subsequent commits only wrapped or moved that sink: CASSANDRA-4669 extracted save_history(); CASSANDRA-5823 relocated the file to ~/.cassandra/cqlsh_history; CASSANDRA-9795 renamed bin/cqlsh to bin/cqlsh.py. Those are not first-writes of the flawed mechanism.
